mcqs.q: How do the social determinants of health (SDH) primarily affect companion animal welfare, per this paper?
o: Indirectly, by impacting the human guardian who cares for the animal
Only through genetic factors in the animal
They have no demonstrated relationship to welfare
mcqs.e: The paper argues SDH impact humans, which in turn directly impacts their companion animals' welfare.

mcqs.q: What does the paper propose to advance companion animal welfare programs?
o: Integrating an SDH framework with the five domains model via multidisciplinary collaboration
mcqs.e: It proposes adapting an SDH framework integrated with the five domains model through multidisciplinary collaboration.

mcqs.q: What research gap does the paper identify?
o: Lack of research on the SDH–animal welfare relationship
Absence of the five domains model
mcqs.e: The paper notes a lack of research specifically exploring the relationship between SDH and animal welfare outcomes.

mcqs.q: What was the estimated social return on investment (SROI) of the RSPCA NSW emergency boarding program?
mcqs.e: The estimated SROI was AUD 8.21 for each AUD 1 invested.

mcqs.q: Which stakeholder groups experienced the bulk of the program's benefit?
mcqs.e: Clients and their animals experienced the bulk of the benefit, valued at over AUD 5 million.

mcqs.q: What does the study conclude about keeping people together with their pets during crisis?
o: It reduces stressors and improves outcomes for people and animals
mcqs.e: The study concludes that keeping people with their pets, or reuniting them quickly, reduces stressors and improves outcomes.

mcqs.q: Which three themes were incorporated into the working definition of a veterinary care desert?
mcqs.e: The review identified accessibility, affordability, and availability as the three common themes.

mcqs.q: At what geographic level was the veterinary care desert definition parameterized?
mcqs.e: The definition was parameterized at the level of census tracts using publicly available data.

mcqs.q: What is the practical clinical relevance of the established definition?
o: To identify areas with reduced access and target interventions
To rank veterinary clinics by quality
mcqs.e: Providers can use census tract data and the definition to identify under-served areas and target interventions.

mcqs.q: Which species received over half of the AMCTTR funds awarded?
mcqs.e: Over half of the US$612,564 awarded went to cats.

mcqs.q: Feline applications were most commonly submitted for which services?
mcqs.e: Feline applications were most commonly for ophthalmology or dentistry, unlike dogs.

mcqs.q: Why were expenditures per dog higher than per cat?
o: Dogs were referred for more expensive orthopedic surgery
More dogs than cats were funded
mcqs.e: Expenditures per cat were lower because dogs were referred for more expensive orthopedic surgery.

mcqs.q: What primarily drove semi-owners to transition to full ownership of cats?
o: Feelings of responsibility, emotional attachment, and access to free sterilization
mcqs.e: 93% of semi-owners cited responsibility, emotional attachment, and access to free sterilization as drivers.

mcqs.q: What proportion of surveyed cats were under 12 months of age?
mcqs.e: Most cats (79%) were under 12 months old.

mcqs.q: What did the study find about prior veterinary care among these cats?
o: Veterinary care was limited, with only 15% having seen a vet
mcqs.e: Veterinary care was limited; only 15% had visited a veterinarian and 28% were vaccinated.

mcqs.q: Which two vector-borne diseases were the focus of this survey of homeless-services staff?
o: Louse-borne Bartonella quintana infection and flea-borne murine typhus
mcqs.e: The study targeted louse-borne Bartonella quintana and flea-borne murine typhus.

mcqs.q: What did the survey reveal about staff knowledge of these diseases?
o: Most staff could accurately name the diseases and protocols
Significant knowledge gaps, with fewer than a quarter able to describe a management protocol
Knowledge was adequate but prevention was over-applied
mcqs.e: The study found significant knowledge gaps; less than a quarter could describe an appropriate management protocol.

mcqs.q: Which harmful misconception did staff hold?
o: That lice and fleas are harmless
That clients must isolate or be denied services until medically cleared
That all clients should be vaccinated
mcqs.e: A misconception was that clients must isolate or be denied services, risking unnecessary service restrictions.

mcqs.q: What did this study conclude about how low-income clients perceive their pets' quality of life?
o: They perceive it more negatively than affluent owners
They perceive QoL similarly to demographics in prior research and are similarly bonded
They could not articulate any QoL themes
They valued QoL but not the human-animal bond
mcqs.e: Lower-income clients perceived QoL similarly to prior research and were similarly bonded and attentive.

mcqs.q: How did the single-item 10-point QoL scale perform across demographics?
o: It differentiated demographics at a statistically significant level
It did not differentiate between demographics significantly
It only worked for English speakers
mcqs.e: The single-item QoL scale did not differentiate demographics at a statistically significant level.

mcqs.q: What measurement do the results support including in pet QoL research?
mcqs.e: Results support the importance of measuring the human-animal bond when researching pet QoL.

mcqs.q: Which resource did Colorado pet owners rate as most helpful for access to care?
o: Low-cost clinics providing sick and emergency care
mcqs.e: Low-cost clinics providing sick and emergency care were rated the most helpful resource by pet owners.

mcqs.q: Which policy efforts did veterinary professionals especially support?
o: Reducing the number of veterinary schools
Recruitment and retention of technicians, including scope clarification and loan repayment
mcqs.e: Professionals especially supported technician recruitment/retention via scope clarification, loan repayment, and career pathways.

mcqs.q: What was pet owners' general attitude toward telemedicine?
o: Generally supportive and comfortable, even for first visits
mcqs.e: Pet owners were generally supportive of telemedicine and comfortable using it even for a first visit.

mcqs.q: Which barrier to accessing veterinary care was most frequently reported in this scoping review?
mcqs.e: Financial limitations were the most frequently reported barrier (n = 57).

mcqs.q: What did the review find about how 'access' to veterinary care is defined in the literature?
o: It is consistently and clearly defined
It lacks a consistent definition, with few publications defining it
It is defined only in livestock contexts
mcqs.e: Access lacks a consistent definition; only 10 publications defined it, prompting a proposed definition.

mcqs.q: After financial limitations, which barriers were most frequently reported?
mcqs.e: Geographic location (n = 35) and limited personnel/equipment (n = 32) were the next most frequent barriers.

mcqs.q: Which theme emerged regarding homeless individuals with serious illness and animal companions?
o: Animals were uniformly a barrier to all care
Some chose animal companionship over formal housing and health services
Animals provided no benefit during illness
Most surrendered animals immediately upon diagnosis
mcqs.e: A major theme was choosing animal companionship over formal housing and health services.

mcqs.q: What analytic approach was used in this study?
mcqs.e: The subsamples were analyzed using an interpretive description approach.

mcqs.q: What overall picture did the study give of animal companionship during serious illness while homeless?
o: Both healing benefits and situations where consequences outweigh benefits
mcqs.e: Themes captured both healing benefits and instances where companionship's consequences outweighed the benefits.

mcqs.q: How did most participants become aware of charitable support for their pets?
mcqs.e: Most participants only became aware of charitable pet support via word-of-mouth.

mcqs.q: What commonly prompted participants to seek charitable veterinary support?
o: A pet health issue or emergency with unaffordable, unanticipated costs
mcqs.e: Seeking support was often triggered by a health emergency with unanticipated, unaffordable veterinary costs.

mcqs.q: Beyond hardship, what did the participants' accounts also highlight?
o: Resilience and strategies that mitigated future crises
A desire to relinquish their pets
mcqs.e: The accounts highlighted how resilience and coping strategies were established, mitigating future crises.

mcqs.q: What was the main finding regarding the physical health of dogs belonging to homeless persons?
o: They were generally well cared for and physically healthy
mcqs.e: Dogs of homeless persons were found to be well cared for and physically healthy, consistent with other studies.

mcqs.q: Which behavioural issue did the dogs notably display?
o: Evidence of separation distress when the owner was away
mcqs.e: The dogs had few behavioural problems but displayed evidence of separation distress while the owner was away.

mcqs.q: What policy change did the study suggest its findings could support?
o: Revising homeless-shelter policies that prohibit dogs staying with their owners
Mandatory surrender of pets at intake
Requiring pet insurance for homeless owners
mcqs.e: Findings could inform changes to policies prohibiting dogs from staying with owners at homeless shelters.
